title: SOP for Code of Conduct
html:
1. Purpose

To establish a uniform Code of Conduct (COC) for all employees, medical professionals, and contractual staff of the hospital in alignment with NABH standards, ensuring ethical, professional, and responsible behavior in all patient care and organizational activities.

2. Scope

This SOP applies to:

  • All hospital employees (clinical & non-clinical)
  • Consultants and visiting doctors
  • Nursing and paramedical staff
  • Administrative and support staff
  • Outsourced/contractual employees and trainees

3. Responsibility

RoleResponsibility
HR DepartmentOrientation, dissemination, and maintenance of COC records
Department HeadsEnsuring compliance within their teams
Quality DepartmentMonitoring adherence as per NABH guidelines
All Staff MembersUnderstanding and complying with the COC at all times

4. Policy Statement

The hospital is committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity, ethics, and professionalism in all interactions — with patients, attendants, colleagues, and the community. Every individual is responsible for upholding the hospital’s reputation and NABH ethical standards.

5. Code of Conduct Guidelines

5.1 Ethical Behavior

  • Maintain honesty, integrity, and fairness in all actions.
  • Avoid any form of corruption, bribery, or malpractice.
  • Do not solicit or accept gifts, commissions, or favors from patients or vendors.

5.2 Professional Conduct

  • Display appropriate behavior and communication with patients, attendants, and coworkers.
  • Respect patient rights, privacy, and dignity at all times.
  • Follow dress code, ID display, and grooming policies.
  • Refrain from using abusive or discriminatory language.
  • Adhere to hospital timings, attendance, and punctuality.

5.3 Confidentiality

  • Protect all patient information and hospital data as per Information Security & Patient Rights policies.
  • Avoid sharing confidential information verbally, electronically, or via social media.
  • Follow HIPAA/NABH confidentiality norms.

5.4 Conflict of Interest

  • Disclose any personal, financial, or professional interests that may conflict with hospital duties.
  • Avoid referral or commission-based practices.

5.5 Compliance with Laws and Regulations

  • Follow all applicable laws, NABH standards, and hospital policies.
  • Report any suspected violation or malpractice immediately to HR/Quality.

5.6 Safety and Security

  • Comply with infection control, biomedical waste management, and safety protocols.
  • Ensure workplace safety for self and others.
  • Report incidents, near misses, or hazards promptly.

5.7 Patient-Centric Approach

  • Always act in the best interest of the patient.
  • Provide care without discrimination based on religion, caste, gender, or financial status.
  • Obtain informed consent and ensure patient education.

5.8 Substance Abuse & Misconduct

  • Consumption or possession of alcohol, narcotics, or tobacco in hospital premises is strictly prohibited.
  • Physical assault, harassment, or discrimination of any form is a gross misconduct.

5.9 Use of Hospital Property

  • Use hospital assets (equipment, vehicles, systems) responsibly.
  • Unauthorized removal or misuse of hospital property will invite disciplinary action.

5.10 Social Media Conduct

  • Do not share hospital-related content, patient images, or confidential information online without authorization.
  • Maintain professionalism in all public communications.

6. Disciplinary Actions

Violations of this Code of Conduct will result in disciplinary action based on the severity of the offense, which may include:

  • Verbal/Written Warning
  • Suspension
  • Termination of Employment

7. Reporting Violations

Employees can report unethical or inappropriate behavior confidentially to:

  • HR Department
  • Quality Department
  • Ethics/Grievance Committee

8. Training and Communication

  • All employees will undergo Code of Conduct orientation during induction.
  • Annual refresher sessions will be conducted.
  • Acknowledgment form to be signed and filed in the HR record.

9. Record Keeping

  • HR maintains records of COC acknowledgments and any disciplinary actions for minimum 3 years.
  • Quality Department monitors compliance during internal audits.
